name: Installed font detection (and Flash fonts)
plain: Measures text width to guess which fonts are installed.
meaning: Font lists reflect installed apps, languages and OS version. Flash font enumeration was another method before Flash ended in 2020.

web.api: Measure text in offscreen elements; Flash getFontList (obsolete)

limits.headline: Can measure text widths to guess which fonts are on your device
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Compare text width across many font names
Learn your system, languages and sometimes installed apps
cannot: Use the old Flash method, which ended in 2020
Know who you are by itself

story.what_it_is: A script measures text width to guess which fonts are installed on your device.

marketing.name: Local Font Access API
marketing.pitch: Chrome offers a permission based way for apps to read installed fonts, instead of guessing by measuring.

story.for_you: You see no sign of it. The page tries many fonts and measures the text, so it knows which ones you have. People with design or office apps tend to have a more unusual list.
story.for_makers: Sites use font checks to decide what to load and to match designs. Ad tech and fraud teams use the font list as a classic trait to tell devices apart.

use_cases.example: A web design tool lists the fonts on your computer so you can use them in your design.
A document editor shows which fonts it will substitute because they are not on your device.
An ad script records which fonts you have as a part of an anonymous device ID.
A bank's fraud tool compares the font list to the last visit to see if it is the same machine.
A site loads its own web font only if a close match is missing, to speed up the page.
A visitor tool separates Mac and Windows users partly by the default fonts found.
A browser game with a text editor for custom names lists fonts so players can style a team badge.

technical_bounds: Some browsers limit fonts to a fixed list
